title: Tenant and route adaptive profile recommender + safe apply pipeline
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background: We need an automated, low-risk way to reduce per-token cost by recommending and applying batching and KV-cache profiles at the per-tenant and per-route level. Current ops are manual: SREs or PMs craft one-off batching profiles and apply via config changes with limited canarying. That causes long lead times and occasional regressions for high-SLO customers.

Proposal: Build an Adaptive Profile Recommender (APR) that analyzes telemetry for a tenant+route, synthesizes a prioritized set of safe candidate config changes (batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, kv_cache_policy, prefix_cache_ttl, quantization_profile_hint), and surfaces them in Console for review. APR will include a Safe Apply Pipeline: dry-run simulation, shadow canary (traffic duplication), automated metric checks, and automated rollback. The pipeline must support per-tenant allowlist/denylist and tier-based guardrails (e.g., enterprise tenants opt-out by default).

Key behaviors:
- Per-customer profiles: keep suggested changes scoped to tenant and route selectors; allow pinning/exclusions for specific customers or paths.
- Route segmentation: use route labels and traffic signatures to recommend narrower or wider batching windows.
- Tier controls: treat premium/enterprise routes as opt-out unless explicit approval given; sandbox for dev/test tenants.
- Safety-first: every suggested change must be accompanied by an estimated cost delta, latency P50/P95 change estimate, and a confidence score (based on data volume of recent traces).

Why different from existing work: Existing tickets focus on policy engines and segmented batching; this ticket bundles a recommendation engine + a structured safe-apply pipeline with canary automation and console UX for human-in-the-loop approval. It also adds a small simulation harness to surface expected changes before any production traffic is touched.
acceptance_criteria: APR generates recommendations for >90% of routes with >= 24 hours of traffic data and includes cost delta estimate, latency delta estimate, and confidence score.
Console UI shows change diff, per-tenant rollback button, and CTA to start Safe Apply pipeline (dry-run -> shadow canary -> apply with realtime checks).

Safe Apply pipeline executes a shadow canary for a selected tenant+route and runs automated metric gates (latency P95, error rate, structured-output fidelity) and will automatically rollback if any gate trips within the canary window.
Enterprise-tagged tenants are excluded from automatic apply by default; approval flow exists for exceptions.
End-to-end e2e tests for dry-run simulation and canary rollback exist in the CI (GitHub PR linked).
tasks: Data pipeline: aggregate per-route/tenant telemetry and compute features (seq length distribution, tokens/request, p50/p95 latency baseline, cold start fraction).
Recommendation engine: model rules + heuristic scorer to propose candidate batching and kv_cache configs with confidence and expected cost/latency deltas.
Dry-run simulator: replay recent traffic against candidate config in a sandboxed runner and produce estimates (cost & latency).
Safe Apply: implement shadow canary path + metric gate runner + automated rollback logic in runtime controller.
Console: add recommendation card, diff view, approval flow, and per-tenant allowlist/denylist controls.
Policy: add tier-based defaults and an enterprise opt-out flag to the config layer.
Tests & monitoring: synthetic canary tests and alerting for failed applies and rollbacks; add dashboard and log links.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Recommendations may degrade structured-output quality for some routes. Mitigation: require structured-output fidelity gate that compares schema/intent-preserving metrics in canary before apply.
Risk: Small-volume tenants produce noisy estimates. Mitigation: only produce high-confidence recommendations when >N requests in window; otherwise surface as 'manual suggestion' for ops review.
Risk: Automatic rollback false positives. Mitigation: two-stage gates — soft alert + hard rollback with a short cooldown and human override in Console.
Risk: Security/compliance for Private deployments. Mitigation: Safe Apply pipeline can be disabled per-deployment; Private customers can require manual approval via RBAC.
notes: Design decision (2026-02-18): we prefer a deterministic heuristic scorer initially; ML-driven ranking considered for H2 after 2 months of telemetry.
Trade-off: tighter batching windows give cost wins but increase tail latency; we will bias recommendations toward conservative latency-preserving configs for premium routes.
Operational playbook: when auto-rollback triggers, the controller files a ticket and notifies the on-call SRE channel with a summary and link to rollback artifacts.
